text:
alex: Quick Q — should rollout metadata include an opaque 'sentinel' that clients can use to detect stale pins vs relying on TTL? trying to handle cross-region pin flips.
jen: short answer: yes for server-side detect, but be careful exposing internals to clients.
dave: i'm thinking something like:
```json
"rollout": {
  "sentinel": "uuid-v4",
  "sentinel_visibility": "public|private",
  "ttl_seconds": 3600
}
```
jen: sentinel_visibility=public lets clients probe, private means only control plane can see; public increases coupling.
lisa: product concern: clients reading sentinels could cause tight coupling; need migration window and opt-in.
ops-bot: deploy note: schema-v2 rollout-meta pushed to staging cluster on 172.16.5.4 (automated)
maria: alternative: keep sentinel opaque but add `client_hint_version` integer that increments on incompatible changes.
dave: +1 to client_hint_version. also propose we model ttl as an explicit enum to avoid magic numbers. e.g. `ttl_kind` = finite|sticky|infinite and ttl_seconds only used when finite.
jen: agree, finite enum avoids folklore like 0/ -1. also we should document migration: control plane will accept old payloads for 90 days and emit a deprecation header.
alex: ok action items: update spec with `sentinel`, `sentinel_visibility`, `client_hint_version`, `ttl_kind`; add backwards-compat tests; prepare migration playbook for dedicated + private.
jen: i'll open the RFC follow-up PR and add sample client shim + unit tests, cc @lisa for product acceptance.
lisa: will review and add acceptance criteria.
alex: thanks — i'll draft the ops migration checklist after PR. :thumbsup:
